result.title: A preference for local interaction between layers emerges during training
result.summary: A deep neural network is a stack of layers, and all layers are trained to lower one shared error. A change in one layer can therefore reach every other layer. Because the error is shared by all layers, one would expect the other layers to respond alike, whether they are next to the changed layer or far from it. We find that early in training the response is weak and its order by distance is not stable. As training proceeds, the response grows, and neighboring layers come to respond to changes in each other more strongly than layers further apart, in almost every network. This locality forms during training, although training links every layer to every other. We show this by pushing one layer of a copy of the network at many stages of training and measuring how much of the push reaches each of the other layers. The experiments use 512 five-layer networks trained on modular addition with each of two optimizers, AdamW and stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 512 个五层模加网络上，于训练各阶段对单层施加扰动并测量其传播到其余各层的强度，发现训练早期响应弱且距离次序不稳定，随训练推进相邻层相互响应显著强于远层，即局部性在训练中自发形成。
AI.relevance_reason: 逐层「推一把再看传播」的度量思路可能可供核查 LVR 中深度与位置对 latent 状态贡献分配的影响，以及训练如何塑造层间信息局部化；但该工作纯属机制观测，与视觉多模态推理无直接联系，需较多核查。
